arxiv-2002-00557.title: Bertrand-DR: Improving Text-to-SQL using a Discriminative Re-ranker
arxiv-2002-00557.creator: Amol Kelkar, Rohan Relan, Vaishali Bhardwaj
arxiv-2002-00557.description: Abstract To access data stored in relational databases, users need to understand the database schema and write a query using a query language such as SQL. To simplify this task, text-to-SQL models attempt to translate a user’s natural language question to corresponding SQL query. Recently, several generative text-to-SQL models have been developed.

arxiv-2002-03592.title: Post-comparison mitigation of demographic bias in face recognition using fair score normalization
arxiv-2002-03592.creator: Philipp Terhörst 1 2, Jan Niklas Kolf 2, Naser Damer 1, Florian Kirchbuchner 1 2, Arjan Kuijper 1 2
arxiv-2002-03592.description: Abstract Current face recognition systems achieve high progress on several benchmark tests. Despite this progress, recent works showed that these systems are strongly biased against demographic sub-groups. Consequently, an easily integrable solution is needed to reduce the discriminatory effect of these biased systems.

arxiv-2104-03414.title: PrivateSNN: Privacy-Preserving Spiking Neural Networks
arxiv-2104-03414.creator: Youngeun Kim, Yeshwanth Venkatesha, Priyadarshini Panda
arxiv-2104-03414.description: Abstract How can we bring both privacy and energy-efficiency to a neural system? In this paper, we propose PrivateSNN, which aims to build low-power Spiking Neural Networks (SNNs) from a pre-trained ANN model without leaking sensitive information contained in a dataset.

arxiv-2107-12011.title: From robust tests to Bayes-like posterior distributions Thanks: This project has received funding from the European Union’s Horizon 2020 research and innovation programme under grant agreement N o 811017
arxiv-2107-12011.creator: Yannick BARAUD
arxiv-2107-12011.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Yannick BARAUD. In the Bayes paradigm, given a loss function and an n n -sample, we present the construction of a new type of posterior distribution, that extends the classical Bayes one. The loss functions we have in mind are either those derived from the total variation and Hellinger distances or some 𝕃 j {\mathbb{L}}_{j} -ones for j > 1 j>1 .

arxiv-2111-02921.title: Map-Assisted Constellation Design for mmWave WDM with OAM in Short-Range LOS Environment
arxiv-2111-02921.creator: Yuan Wang, Chen Gong, Nuo Huang, Zhengyuan Xu
arxiv-2111-02921.description: Abstract We consider a system that integrates positioning and single-user millimeter wave (mmWave) communication, where the communication part adopts wavelength division multiplexing (WDM) and orbital angular momentum (OAM). This paper addresses the multi-dimensional constellation design in short-range line-of-sight (LOS) environment, with stable communication links.

arxiv-2111-15345.title: Binary-object spectral-synthesis in 3D ( BOSS-3D )
arxiv-2111-15345.creator: L. Hennicker, N. D. Kee, T. Shenar, J. Bodensteiner, M. Abdul-Masih, I. El Mellah, H. Sana, J. O. Sundqvist
arxiv-2111-15345.description: Abstract Context. To quantitatively decode the information stored within an observed spectrum, detailed modelling of the physical state and accurate radiative transfer solution schemes are required. The accuracy of the model is then typically evaluated by comparing the calculated and observed spectra.

arxiv-2204-14202.title: Resonant tunneling diodes in semiconductor microcavities: modeling polaritonic features in the THz displacement current
arxiv-2204-14202.creator: Carlos F. Destefani 1, Matteo Villani 1, Xavier Cartoixà 1, Michael Feiginov 2, Xavier Oriols 1
arxiv-2204-14202.description: Abstract We develop in this work a simple qualitative quantum electron transport model, in the strong light-matter coupling regime under dipole approximation, able to capture polaritonic signatures in the time-dependent electrical current. The effect of the quantized electromagnetic field in the displacement current of a resonant tunneling diode inside an optical cavity is analyzed.

arxiv-2212-07290.title: Gravitational transition form factors of N → Δ N\rightarrow\Delta via QCD light-cone sum rules
arxiv-2212-07290.creator: U. Özdem, K. Azizi
arxiv-2212-07290.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by U. Özdem, K. Azizi. We present the first direct calculation on the gravitational form factors (GFFs) of the N → Δ N\rightarrow\Delta transition using an analytic method, the QCD light-cone sum rules. The matrix element of the quark part of the energy momentum tensor current sandwiched between the nucleon and Δ \Delta states are parameterized in terms of five independent conserved and four independent non-conserved GFFs, for calculation of which we use the distribution amplitudes (DAs) of the on-shell nucleon expanded in terms of

arxiv-2302-07036.title: SCONNA: A Stochastic Computing Based Optical Accelerator for Ultra-Fast, Energy-Efficient Inference of Integer-Quantized CNNs
arxiv-2302-07036.creator: Sairam Sri Vatsavai, Venkata Sai Praneeth Karempudi, Ishan Thakkar, Ahmad Salehi, and Todd Hastings
arxiv-2302-07036.description: Abstract Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) are used extensively for artificial intelligence applications due to their record-breaking accuracy. For efficient and swift hardware-based acceleration, CNNs are typically quantized to have integer input/weight parameters. The acceleration of a CNN inference task uses convolution operations that are typically transformed into vector-dot-product (VDP) operations.

arxiv-2310-04195.title: Nonzero Spatial Curvature in Symmetric Teleparallel Cosmology
arxiv-2310-04195.creator: Andronikos Paliathanasis
arxiv-2310-04195.description: Abstract We consider the symmetric teleparallel f ⁡ ( Q ) f\left(Q\right) -gravity in Friedmann–Lemaître–Robertson–Walker cosmology with nonzero spatial curvature. For a nonlinear f ⁡ ( Q ) f\left(Q\right) model there exist always the limit of General Relativity with or without the cosmological constant term.

arxiv-2406-02436.title: Safe, Out-of-Distribution-Adaptive MPC with Conformalized Neural Network Ensembles
arxiv-2406-02436.creator: Jose Leopoldo Contreras, Ola Shorinwa, Mac Schwager
arxiv-2406-02436.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Jose Leopoldo Contreras, Ola Shorinwa, Mac Schwager. We present SODA-MPC, a Safe, Out-of-Distribution-Adaptive Model Predictive Control algorithm that uses an ensemble of learned models for prediction with a runtime monitor to flag unreliable out-of-distribution (OOD) predictions. When an OOD situation is detected, SODA-MPC triggers a safe fallback control strategy based on reachability, producing a control framework that achieves the high performance of learning-based models while preserving the safety of reachability-based control.

arxiv-2411-01666.title: Normality criterion for a family of holomorphic curves that partially share wandering hyperplanes with their derivatives, and holomorphic functions lifted to curves in ℙ 2 ​ ( ℂ ) \mathbb{P}^{2}(\mathbb{C})
arxiv-2411-01666.creator: Sonam Mehta, Kuldeep Singh Charak
arxiv-2411-01666.description: Abstract In this paper we generalize a result of Ye, Pang and Yang [ 12 ] on the normality of a family of holomorphic curves in ℙ N ​ ( ℂ ) \mathbb{P}^{N}(\mathbb{C}) . Further we obtain a normality criteria for family of meromorphic functions that partially share wandering holomorphic functions with their derivatives.

arxiv-2502-20437.title: Introducing the thesan-zoom project: radiation-hydrodynamic simulations of high-redshift galaxies with a multi-phase interstellar medium
arxiv-2502-20437.creator: Rahul Kannan, 1⋆ Ewald Puchwein, 2 Aaron Smith, 3 Josh Borrow, 4 Enrico Garaldi, 5,6 Laura Keating, 7 Mark Vogelsberger, 8 Oliver Zier, 9,8 William McClymont, 10,11 Xuejian Shen, 8 Filip Popovic, 1 Sandro Tacchella, 10,11 Lars Hernquist, 9 and Volker Springel 12
arxiv-2502-20437.description: Abstract We introduce the thesan-zoom project, a comprehensive suite of high-resolution zoom-in simulations of 14 14 high-redshift ( z > 3 z>3 ) galaxies selected from the thesan simulation volume. This sample encompasses a diverse range of halo masses, with M halo ≈ 10 8 − 10 13 ​ M ☉ M_{\mathrm{halo}}\approx 10^{8}-10^{13}\penalty\ \text{M}_{\astrosun} at z = 3 z=3 .

arxiv-2506-02518.title: Prenatal phthalate exposures and adiposity outcomes trajectories: a multivariate Bayesian factor regression approach
arxiv-2506-02518.creator: Phuc Nguyen, Stephanie M. Engel, Amy H. Herring
arxiv-2506-02518.description: Abstract We aim to assess the longitudinal effects of prenatal exposure to phthalates on the risk of childhood obesity in children aged 4 to 7, with potential time-varying and sex-specific effects. Multiple body-composition-related outcomes, such as BMI z-score, fat mass percentage, and waist circumference, are available in the data.

arxiv-2507-04218.title: DreamPoster: A Unified Framework for Image-Conditioned Generative Poster Design
arxiv-2507-04218.creator: Xiwei Hu 1,∗ Haokun Chen 1,∗ Zhongqi Qi 1,∗ Hui Zhang 1,2,∗ Dexiang Hong 1 Jie Shao 1,† Xinglong Wu 1
arxiv-2507-04218.description: Abstract We present DreamPoster, a Text-to-Image generation framework that intelligently synthesizes high-quality posters from user-provided images and text prompts while maintaining content fidelity and supporting flexible resolution and layout outputs. Specifically, DreamPoster is built upon our T2I model, Seedream3.0 [ 9 ] to uniformly process different poster generating types.

arxiv-2601-00664.title: Avatar Forcing: Real-Time Interactive Head Avatar Generation for Natural Conversation
arxiv-2601-00664.creator: Taekyung Ki Sangwon Jang Jaehyeong Jo Jaehong Yoon Sung Ju Hwang
arxiv-2601-00664.description: A 2026 arXiv research paper by Taekyung Ki Sangwon Jang Jaehyeong Jo Jaehong Yoon Sung Ju Hwang. Talking head generation creates lifelike avatars from static portraits for virtual communication and content creation. However, current models do not yet convey the feeling of truly interactive communication, often generating one-way responses that lack emotional engagement. We identify two key challenges toward truly interactive avatars: generating motion in real-time under causal constraints and learning expressive, vibrant reactions without additional labeled data.

govdocs-nsarchive-News_foia_Archive_Hist.title: Archive, Historians, CREW Sue White House, Seek to Preserve Presidential Records During the Transition
govdocs-nsarchive-News_foia_Archive_Hist.creator: National Security Archive
govdocs-nsarchive-News_foia_Archive_Hist.description: Washington, D.C., Dec. 1, 2020 – The National Security Archive, the Society for Historians of American Foreign Relations, the American Historical Association, and the Citizens for Responsibility and Ethics in Washington today filed suit against President Donald Trump in his official capacity, seeking to enforce the Presidential Records Act and prevent any destruction of records during the presidential transition.

joseph-conrad.title: Joseph Conrad
joseph-conrad.creator: Walpole, Hugh
joseph-conrad.description: Excerpt from Joseph Conrad Looking for an instant at the dramatic contrast and almost ironical relationship of these three backgrounds - Poland, the Sea, the inner security and tradition of an English country-side - one can realise what they may make of an artist. That early Polish atmosphere, viewed through all the deep light and high shade of a remembered childhood. May be enough to give life...

pmc-10536711.title: Sound Absorption Performance and Mechanical Properties of the 3D-Printed Bio-Degradable Panels
pmc-10536711.creator: Sebastian-Marian Zaharia, Mihai Alin Pop, Mihaela Cosnita, Cătălin Croitoru, Simona Matei, Cosmin Spîrchez, Santiago Ferrandiz, Dana Luca Motoc
pmc-10536711.description: The 3D printing process allows complex structures to be obtained with low environmental impact using biodegradable materials. This work aims to develop and acoustically characterize 3D-printed panels using three types of materials, each manufactured at five infill densities (20%, 40%, 60%, 80% and 100%) with three internal configurations based on circular, triangular, and corrugated profiles.

pmc-11503044.title: Safety and efficacy of aceneuramic acid in GNE myopathy: open-label extension study
pmc-11503044.creator: Naoki Suzuki, Madoka Mori-Yoshimura, Masahisa Katsuno, Masanori P Takahashi, Satoshi Yamashita, Yasushi Oya, Atsushi Hashizume, Shinichiro Yamada, Masayuki Nakamori, Rumiko Izumi, Masaaki Kato, Hitoshi Warita, Maki Tateyama, Hiroshi Kuroda, Ryuta Asada, Takuhiro Yamaguchi, Ichizo Nishino, Masashi Ao
pmc-11503044.description: progressive decrease in muscle strength, starting from the distal parts of the arms and legs.1 Patients with GNE myopathy have mutations in the GNE gene encoding a bifunctional enzyme involved in sialic acid (SA) biosynthesis.2 GNE mutations decrease SA production, leading to hyposialylation and eventually to disease onset.

pmc-12512922.title: Advancing the women’s health strategy: a policy lab aimed at improving effective management of hyperemesis gravidarum
pmc-12512922.creator: Melanie Nana, Tianne Haggar, Harriet Boulding, Ross Pow, Catherine Nelson-Piercy, Catherine Williamson
pmc-12512922.description: BackgroundHyperemesis gravidarum (HG) is associated with morbidity and mortality which can be exacerbated by difficulties accessing guideline-recommended treatment. Improving outcomes for women with HG through policy and practice fulfils the vision of the Women’s Health Strategy for England. We aimed to align with the Women’s Health Strategy by addressing barriers to evidence-based care and to improve effective management of HG.

pmc-12570531.title: Patients’ views on a subsidy card model for gluten-free food access: a qualitative study
pmc-12570531.creator: Abubakar Sha’aban, Francesca Mazzaschi, Elizabeth Doe, Beti-Jane Ingram, Alison Jones, Emma Williams, Heather O’Sullivan, Andrew Evans, Adrian Edwards, Natalie Joseph-Williams
pmc-12570531.description: BackgroundCoeliac disease requires strict adherence to a gluten-free diet to prevent health complications. While gluten-free foods (GFF) are traditionally available on the National Health Service (NHS) prescriptions, the cost and limited product range have prompted consideration of alternatives. Wales is exploring replacing prescriptions with a subsidy card scheme, piloted and implemented by the Hywel Dda University Health Board.

pmc-12574492.title: COVID‐19 Vaccine Mistrust, Racial Discrimination, and Conspiracy Beliefs Among Parents in Canada: Implications for Public Health
pmc-12574492.creator: Rose Darly Dalexis, Yan Xu, Seyed Mohammad Mahdi Moshirian Farahi, Idrissa Beogo, Mwali Muray, Jude Mary Cénat
pmc-12574492.description: Despite studies documenting the evolution and factors related to COVID‐19 vaccination in Canadian children, gaps in research on COVID‐19 vaccine mistrust (VM) across ethnocultural groups hinder tailored public health responses. This study examines the sociodemographic characteristics and factors related to COVID‐19 VM among racially diverse Canadian parents with children aged 0–12 years from Arab, Asian, Black, Indigenous, and White communities.

pmc-12605714.title: Clinical and translational study of ivosidenib plus nivolumab in advanced solid tumors harboring IDH1 mutations
pmc-12605714.creator: Matthew K Nguyen, Mark Jelinek, Arjun Singh, Brian Isett, Erica S Myers, Steven J Mullett, Yvonne Eisele, Jan H Beumer, Robert A Parise, Julie Urban, Amy Rose, Lorenzo Sellitto, Krishna Singh, Rose Doerfler, Rebekah E Dadey, Carl Kim, John C Rhee, Diwakar Davar, Liza C Villaruz, Melissa Burgess, Jan
pmc-12605714.description: BackgroundCancers that do not respond to immunotherapy typically harbor a non-T cell-inflamed tumor microenvironment (TME), characterized by the absence of type I/II interferon signaling and CD8+ T cell infiltration. We previously reported IDH1 somatic mutations were enriched in this phenotype across histologies.

pmc-12615654.title: Proteomics characterization of triple-negative apocrine carcinoma reveals molecular features of progression and chemotherapy response
pmc-12615654.creator: Yiying Zhu, Mengping Long, Wenhao Shi, Tianlong He, Fangzhou Xie, Annan Qian, Yuqiao Liu, Taobo Hu, Shaojun Tang
pmc-12615654.description: Triple-negative apocrine carcinoma (TNAC) is a rare and chemotherapy-insensitive subtype of triple-negative breast cancer (TNBC), characterized by specific morphology and molecular features. Despite limited chemotherapy response, TNAC shows favorable long-term survival, suggesting distinct resistance mechanisms. In this study, we present the first proteomics-based profiling of TNAC formalin-fixed paraffin-embedded (FFPE) samples using mass spectrometry.

pmc-12658235.title: Methylene blue treatment of fatal cerebral malaria and identification of potential blood biomarkers
pmc-12658235.creator: Jing Wen Hang, Yew Wai Leong, Vipin Narang, Piyanate Sunyakumthorn, Rawiwan Im-Erbsin, Shihui Foo, Josephine Lum, Bernett Lee, Arthur E Brown, Laurent Rénia, Gareth D H Turner, Samuel C Wassmer, Eric D Lombardini, Bruce Russell, Benoît Malleret
pmc-12658235.description: Cerebral malaria (CM) is a severe complication caused by Plasmodium falciparum infection, leading to persistent neurological impairments in survivors. To understand the complex mechanisms and investigate advanced diagnostic and treatment strategies targeting human CM, we utilize Plasmodium coatneyi-infected male rhesus macaques, a non-human primate model closely resembling P. falciparum infection in humans.

pmc-12960758.title: Introduction to the Special Issue: Prevalence and Characteristics of Child Sexual Abuse Perpetration in Australia, the United States, and United Kingdom
pmc-12960758.creator: Michael Salter, Delanie Woodlock, Tyson Whitten
pmc-12960758.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). This special issue presents findings from the largest multi-country study of men’s self-reported sexual interest and behaviour towards children, addressing critical gaps in evidence on the prevalence, correlates, and prevention of child sexual exploitation and abuse perpetration.

pmc-13146922.title: ABSTRACT NUMBER: ESOC2026A1434 COMPARISON BETWEEN MANUAL AND AUTOMATED MEASUREMENT OF STROKE THROMBOLYSIS WORKFLOW METRICS
pmc-13146922.creator: Cameron Brown, Mostafa Abdou, Keith Muir
pmc-13146922.description: Background and aimsAudit of thrombolysis workflow for performance monitoring often requires manual review of health records. We investigated whether automated processing of routinely collected electronic health record (EHR) data could provide reliable workflow metrics in a comprehensive stroke centre.MethodsA locally developed web-based electronic proforma (StrokeApp) is used for real-time clinical documentation.

pmc-13407287.title: 昼夜节律、肥胖与炎症的交互作用及运动调控
pmc-13407287.creator: Danni CAO, Peizhen ZHANG, 旭芳 吴
pmc-13407287.description: 昼夜节律是人体内在的、24 h的生理活动节律，其紊乱与肥胖和慢性炎症密切相关。生物钟基因不仅调控代谢过程，也参与炎症反应的调节。生物钟失调可导致节律紊乱、肥胖与炎症之间的恶性循环。规律的运动可以作为一种有效的“时间调节器”，帮助调整紊乱的生物节律，并降低与肥胖相关的炎症水平。运动效果可能受运动时间、强度等因素的影响，如不同时段运动对血糖和睡眠的改善作用有所差异。然而，目前尚不清楚针对生物钟已经失调的个体，是否存在一个普遍适用的“最佳”运动时间。系统梳理并总结昼夜节律、肥胖与炎症之间的相互作用机制，并揭示运动在调节生物钟、减轻炎症方面的潜在价值，对制订运动干预策略具有重要意义。未来研究可进一步探索个性化运动处方的制订，特别是针对轮班工作者等高危人群，以推动“时间医学”在代谢健康管理中的应用。Keywords: 昼夜节律, 肥胖, 炎症, 运动, 时间疗法 生命是一个周期化的过程，这种周期化并非简单的重复，而是一种动态的、有方向的振荡，其总体趋势是走向衰老。但在整个生命的大周期中，又蕴含着无数个小周期来维持其整体的稳定与延续[1]。昼夜节律是指频率为一天(24 h)的生命活动节律，由内在时钟驱动，并受到许多外在因素影响[2]。然而，随着现代生活方式的改变，昼夜节律紊乱已成为全球性的健康隐患[3]，这种节律紊乱可能加剧代谢失调并放大不良生活方式带来的负面影响。 随着社会经济的发展和饮食、睡眠、运动等生活方式的改变，肥胖在中国已成为重大公共卫生问题。预计到2030年，中国成人超重和肥胖的患病率将达65.3%，学龄儿童和青少年的患病率将达31.8%[4]。在肥胖状态下，脂肪组织成为全身低度炎症的主要来源：一方面，脂肪分泌大量促炎性脂肪因子，包括肿瘤坏死因子-α(tumor necrosis factor-alpha，TNF-α)、白细胞介素(interleukin，IL)-6、IL-1等；另一方面，脂联素(adiponectin，APN)等抗炎脂肪因子的分泌减少；同时，脂肪组织中巨噬细胞浸润显著增加，进一步释放炎症因子，形成正反馈循环，加剧局部和全身炎症[5]。 运动作为一种有效的节律调节器和抗炎干预手段，在缓解肥胖相关炎症中展现出独特作用。规律运动能够在一定程度上改善超重和肥胖人群的炎症状态。Tan等[6]将超重和肥胖的绝经后女性随机分为力量训练组和日常活动组，在经过12周干预后发现：力量训练组的C反应蛋白水平较干预前下降了21.3%，2组间的TNF-α水平也存在显著差异，且日常活动组的APN水平显著降低(P<0.01)。上述结果表明，力量训练可能有助于抑制TNF-α水平的升高和APN水平的下降。值得注意的是，不同运动参数对炎症标志物的影响存在差异[7]，提示运动干预效果可能受个体特征和运动方案的影响。 然而，目前关于运动如何通过调节节律以影响炎症的机制尚未完全阐明，尤其针对昼夜节律紊乱的肥胖人群，仍不明确是否存在“最佳”运动时间窗口或需避免的“禁忌时段”。因此，系统探讨运动在节律-肥胖-炎症轴中的作用路径，对制订个性化运动干预策略具有重要意义。系统梳理昼夜节律紊乱、肥胖和炎症三者之间的相互关系，分析运动干预对昼夜节律紊乱的肥胖患者炎症因子影响的现有证据，阐明其潜在分子机制，有望为未来的研究方向和实践应用提供理论依据。 昼夜节律系统 周期为24 h的连续生命周期的波动变化称为昼夜节律[8]。在哺乳动物中，位于视交叉上核(suprachiasmatic nucleus，SCN)的中央起搏器通过接受光照/黑暗、活动/休息、进食/禁食等外部刺激来激活昼夜节律系统[3]。同时，SCN还通过激素的周期性分泌及自主神经系统来影响身体中的其他生物钟[4]。几乎所有的器官和组织，如肝、脂肪、胰腺、心脏等均拥有自己的昼夜节律钟，它们受SCN的总体协调，但也受局部因素影响，如进食时间，即使SCN节律正常，不规律的进食也会扰乱外周节律[9]。 哺乳动物的生物钟具备自主性，主要由2条相互交织的转录-翻译反馈环路构成[10]。1)核心负反馈环路：由昼夜节律运动输出周期蛋白(circadian locomotor output cycles kaput，CLOCK)与脑和肌肉芳香烃受体核转运样蛋白1(brain and muscle ARNT-like 1，BMAL1)形成异源二聚体，作为转录激活因子发挥调控作用。该二聚体结合到周期蛋白(period，PER)和隐花色素(cryptochrome，CRY)的启动子区域E-box元件上，激活二者转录；PER和CRY蛋白在细胞质中积累、形成复合物后进入细胞核。细胞核内的PER/CRY复合物会抑制CLOCK与BMAL1的转录活性，从而抑制自身的表达，形成一个约24 h的延迟负反馈循环。2)辅助调控环路：CLOCK-BMAL1也可激活过氧化物酶体增殖物激活受体(peroxisome proliferator-activated receptor，PPAR)α、核受体亚家族1D组成员11(nuclear receptor subfamily 1 group D member 1，Nr1d1)和视黄酸相关孤儿受体(retinoic acid-related orphan receptor，ROR)α/β等基因的转录。它们的蛋白质产物可竞争结合BMAL1基因启动子上的ROR反应元件(ROR response element，RORE)：RORα可激活BMAL1转录，而Nr1d1则抑制其转录，由此形成第2个反馈环路，增强整个系统的稳健性和精确性[11]。 昼夜节律与肥胖、炎症的交叉调控 生物钟可以自我维持振荡，但它仍对来自外界的信号保持敏感，以此保持内源性和外界时钟的一致，其失调与多种代谢性疾病密切相关[12]。CLOCK-BMAL1可驱动数千个控制生理过程(如代谢)的时钟调控基因的表达[13]。此外，CRY和PER可以独立于其他核心时钟对其进行补充调节[14]。例如，脂肪细胞BMAL1缺失导致细胞胰岛素敏感性增加，进而抑制脂肪细胞的脂解，导致细胞肥大[15]，而髓系细胞特异性BMAL1缺失会使小鼠易发生与急、慢性炎症相关的病理改变[16]。这可能归因于BMAL1可通过调控染色质可及性、与其他转录因子相互作用，以组织特异性方式结合目标基因[17]。研究[18]显示，夜班工作时长10年以内的工人代谢综合征的患病率为37.5%，而超过10年者患病率为50.0%。此外，睡眠时间越短，体重指数(body mass index，BMI)越倾向于升高[19]；不规律的进食模式不仅增加了总能量摄入，也会进一步增加体重[20]。 肥胖可通过脂肪组织炎症进一步加剧代谢紊乱。中性粒细胞是最早浸润脂肪组织的免疫细胞。研究[21]表明，小鼠高脂饮食(high fat diet，HFD)喂养3 d后，脂肪组织中的中性粒细胞数量显著增加并分泌趋化因子和细胞因子，促进巨噬细胞浸润，引起肥胖导致的胰岛素抵抗和全身低度慢性炎症；此外，中性粒细胞还通过分泌弹性蛋白酶等物质，直接降解胰岛素受体底物1(insulin receptor substrate 1，IRS1)，破坏胰岛素信号。而巨噬细胞作为慢性炎症的主要效应细胞在脂肪组织中大量积聚，并节律性分泌TNF-α和IL-6来促进炎症、维持胰岛素抵抗[22]。 肥胖及相关并发症是由核因子-κB(nuclear factor-kappa pmc-13556400.title: 520. In vitro Metabolism of fentanyl analogues baring extended propionyl chain: 4-Methoxybutyrylfentanyl and 4-Methoxyvalerylfentanyl
pmc-13556400.creator: D Atsumi, R Hiramatsu, K Abe, Y Oida, K Tsukamoto, T Yokoi, T Ito, K Kitaichi
pmc-13556400.description: BackgroundStructurally modified fentanyls, so-called fentanyl analogs (FAs), represent a global public health threat associated with opioid misuse and overdose. Butyrylfentanyl (BF) and valerylfentanyl (VF), which have an extended propionyl chain of fentanyl, are listed as Schedule I substances by the U.S. Drug Enforcement Administration (DEA) and the United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime (UNODC).
